rationale: Round 1 built cleanly with correctness preserved and no ICE fallback, so this candidate raises SecurityGain/DiversityGain across the board while keeping cost weights bounded to protect the hot numeric kernels (Jacobi, QRiterate, Trianglelise, DivideAndSolve are dense iteration loops where FLA/BCF flattening overhead would hurt most). Cheap, low-risk passes SUB and SPLIT get the highest security weights since arithmetic substitution and basic-block splitting add strong static-analysis friction at negligible runtime cost on this 14KB binary. IBR keeps a high weight for opaque control-flow diversity that pairs well with flattened blocks, and ICALL stays moderately high to add indirect-call indirection to the cross-file calls between main, MM, QRfact, and Triang. FLA is held slightly below BCF because full-loop flattening on the large matrix kernels carries the steepest runtime penalty, and IGV is kept moderate with a higher CorrectnessRisk weight since global-variable encodings touch shared state (matrix globals in MM/main) and this program passes data heavily through globals. Overall the table shifts the mix toward cost-cheap passes for blanket coverage while reserving the expensive flatteners for a moderate, function-feature-gated application.
